summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, diastolic heart failure, and depression was admitted for recurrent chest pain and dizziness. Initial evaluation revealed transient chest pain with non-specific EKG changes, but serial troponins were negative and prior stress test was normal, ruling out acute cardiac cause. Dizziness was attributed to orthostatic hypotension, likely exacerbated by dehydration and medication effects. Her creatinine was elevated on admission but normalized with IV hydration. Depression was identified as a contributing factor to her symptoms, and social work was consulted for counseling support. Medications were adjusted, including temporary hold of antihypertensives and reduction of spironolactone. She improved clinically, remained asymptomatic, and was discharged home with follow-up plans.
